content.value_statement: Hardcoded values make code harder to change and can expose secrets. This skill guides reviews toward constants, configuration files, and environment variables.
actual_capabilities: Identifies magic numbers, repeated strings, hardcoded URLs, secrets, timeouts, and ports.
Recommends constants, enums, config files, or environment variables based on value type.
Shows TypeScript examples for organized constants and environment validation.
Provides grep search patterns for hardcoded values in TypeScript projects.
Includes review workflows and a checklist for new features and pull requests.
limitations: Examples are mainly TypeScript and Korean-language guidance.
The skill gives review guidance and does not enforce policy in CI by itself.
The grep examples are simple and may miss values or report harmless matches.
Project-specific exceptions still need human review.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Find hardcoded limits, URLs, statuses, and secrets before changes are merged.

use_cases.title: Build New Features
use_cases.description: Place configurable values in constants, config files, or environment variables from the start.

use_cases.title: Prepare Configuration Cleanup
use_cases.description: Plan a cleanup of repeated values and undocumented environment variables across a repository.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Hardcoding Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one file or small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file for hardcoded values. List magic numbers, repeated strings, URLs, secrets, and suggested replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Guided Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Move values into safer locations without changing behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this feature to move changeable values into constants, config, or environment variables. Preserve behavior and explain each moved value.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess a larger change before merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this pull request for hardcoded credentials, endpoints, ports, and business thresholds. Prioritize findings by security and maintenance impact.

prompt_templates.title: Repository Policy Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a team standard for future changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a no-hardcoding policy for this repository. Include folder placement, naming rules, environment validation, and review checklist items.

output_examples.input: Review a feature file with repeated status strings and numeric limits.
output: Flags repeated status text as a constant candidate.
Recommends named limits for user counts and timeouts.
Notes values that may be acceptable exceptions.

output_examples.input: Audit a pull request that adds API calls and credentials.
output_examples.output: The review highlights hardcoded endpoints, secret-like values, and missing environment documentation.

output_examples.input: Plan configuration for a new integration.
output_examples.output: The response separates public URLs, private keys, retry limits, and timeout values into appropriate configuration locations.

best_practices: Name constants by meaning, not by current value.
Keep secret values in approved secret storage, not source files.
Update environment examples whenever required variables change.
anti_patterns: Leaving repeated status strings in separate modules.
Putting private API keys in client-side configuration.
Using broad search results without reviewing context.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: The skill contains guidance and example search commands. It does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Can it detect real secrets?
faq.answer: It can help find secret-like patterns, but dedicated secret scanning tools should verify results.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript, but the review principles apply to most application code.

faq.question: Will it remove every hardcoded value?
faq.answer: No. Some values are acceptable when their meaning is obvious or conventional.

faq.question: How should environment variables be handled?
faq.answer: Use validation, documentation, and secret storage according to your deployment platform.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex.
